input: Learner level: new library volunteers; use plain language. Concept ‘checked out’: an item currently assigned to a borrower. Approved example: Book A assigned to Mina. Nonexample: Book B on the return cart with no borrower assignment. Concept ‘on shelf’: an item placed in its assigned shelf location. Approved example: Book C at shelf F2. Nonexample: Book D assigned to Jo. Known confusion: volunteers think every item not on a shelf is checked out.

expected_artifact.orientation: Use borrower assignment and assigned-shelf location as separate recognition cues; the supplied information does not establish that the statuses are mutually exclusive.

concepts.name: checked out
non_features: Merely not being on a shelf is not supplied as sufficient

concepts.name: on shelf
defining_features: Placed in its assigned shelf location
non_features: Borrower assignment alone does not establish assigned-shelf placement

boundary_cases.case: Book B is on the return cart with no borrower assignment.
boundary_cases.basis: It is a nonexample of checked out, but the input does not classify it as on shelf.

recognition_cues: Look for a current borrower assignment.
Look for placement at the assigned shelf location.

evidence.source_input: Approved checked-out example: Book A assigned to Mina.
Approved on-shelf example: Book C at shelf F2.

unresolved_ambiguities: The input does not say whether an item can be both assigned to a borrower and placed in its assigned shelf location, so no either-or question is supported.
The status of items that are neither assigned to a borrower nor at their assigned shelf location is not supplied.
